    If you're currently enjoying building your own video library, then Gelato is definitely a tool that will make you exclaim "It's amazing!" It cleverly breaks down the barriers between Jellyfin (local private cloud) and Stremio (online streaming aggregation), combining the advantages of both.

    However, please note that Gelato is not a standalone "web frontend" or "skin"—it is essentially a Jellyfin server plugin. Once installed, it runs directly within Jellyfin, "injecting" the vast content catalog and online streaming capabilities of the Streamio ecosystem into your Jellyfin database, allowing this external content to be browsed, searched, and played like native local media. You don't need to switch client interfaces—continue using your familiar Jellyfin Web UI, Streamyfin, or any Jellyfin-compatible client.

    Simply put, Gelato's slogan is "More Content, Less Hassle" —get more content with less hassle.

    I. What is Gelato?

    Gelato is an open-source Jellyfin plugin maintained by developer lostb1t and hosted on GitHub (repository address: [link to GitHub github.com/lostb1t/Gelato]). Its core function is as a "Jellyfin Stremio Integration Plugin," integrating Jellyfin with the Stremio ecosystem. Specifically, it uses the "super-aggregator plugin" AIOStreams as an intermediary layer to directly import community-driven Stremio content catalogs into your Jellyfin media library.

    Its core value can be summarized in one sentence:

    Jellyfin allows you to simultaneously view movies on your own hard drive and movies from across the internet.

    Gelato's technical positioning

    To help you better understand Gelato's place in the overall technology stack, here's a summary of key concepts:

    Data flow diagram:

    User search/browsing → Jellyfin → Gelato Plugin → AIOStreams → Various Stremio source plugins
                                                            ↓
                                              Debrid service / P2P streaming
                                                            ↓
                                              Return to streaming link → Jellyfin proxy playback

    This means that Gelato is not a tool to replace the Jellyfin frontend, but rather a plugin that enhances the capabilities of the Jellyfin backend. You continue to use whatever Jellyfin client you prefer—the changes happen "behind the scenes."

    II. Core Functional Highlights

    Stremio-powered intelligent search

    This is the most noticeable change in Gelato—it replaces Jellyfin's default search functionality with a search powered by Stremio.

    When you search for a movie in Jellyfin:

    • If the movie is already on your local hard drive → it will be displayed as a local resource normally.
    • If the media is not present locally, Gelato will query the Stremio content directory via AIOStreams (using TMDB as the metadata source by default) and inject the search results directly into the Jellyfin database, making it appear as if the media is already present locally.
    • When you click play, Gelato will retrieve the online playback link from the configured Streamio streaming source (such as Comet, Torrentio, or MediaFusion).

    For example , if you search for "Dune 2," even if it's not on your Jellyfin hard drive, the search results page will still show its full poster, synopsis, and cast information. After clicking play, Gelato uses the underlying Stremio plugin ecosystem to obtain an online streaming link for you, allowing you to play it directly in the Jellyfin player.

    Batch import of catalogs

    In addition to on-demand search, Gelato also supports batch importing of the entire Stremio content catalog via scheduled tasks .

    This means you can:

    • Enable multiple content categories (such as "Popular Movies", "Highly Rated TV Series") from AIOStreams.
    • Gelato will periodically run import tasks in the background, automatically writing the entries from these directories into the Jellyfin database.
    • These entries will appear on your Jellyfin media library homepage and in the recommended list, completely mixed in with local files, making them indistinguishable.

    Important Notes : It's not recommended to use too many directories, as more directories will slow down the import task and introduce a lot of "random content" that you may not be interested in. A better approach is to curate a curated playlist using Trakt or MDBList, add it as a custom plugin in AIOStreams via StremThru, and then import it using Gelato —this ensures content quality while avoiding information overload.

    Streaming proxy

    All of Gelato's online streams are proxied and forwarded through Jellyfin servers . This design brings several very important practical benefits:

    • Debrid Service IP Protection : Debrid services (such as Real-Debrid) have strict restrictions on multi-IP access. Direct connections from multiple devices may result in account bans. By using Jellyfin as a proxy, the debrid service only sees your server's single IP address, fundamentally avoiding this problem.
    • Worry-free multi-device setup : TVs, mobile phones, tablets, computers—all devices in your home are relayed through Jellyfin servers, eliminating the need to configure a Debrid account for each device separately.
    • Remote access friendly : With the help of reverse proxies (such as Nginx and Caddy), you can securely access all content on the external network, including online resources injected by Gelato.

    Per-User Settings

    This is a very useful but easily overlooked feature of Gelato – each Jellyfin user can have an independent AIOStreams configuration (Manifest).

    This leads to the following possibilities:

    • Parental controls : Configure a content-filtered AIOStreams Manifest for children's accounts to display only age-appropriate content.
    • Personalized preferences : Different family members can enable different content sources and filtering rules.
    • Independent Debrid Accounts : If each family member has a Debrid account, they can use their own API Key in their respective configurations.

    This makes Gelato ideal for multi-user family scenarios, where everyone can see a different "unlimited media library".

    Deeply integrated with Jellyfin's native features

    Content injected by Gelato is not "second-class citizens"—it behaves exactly like local files in Jellyfin:

    • Appears in the "Continue Watching" list
    • Support marking as viewed/favorited
    • Appears alongside local files in category browsing and recommendations
    • Supports Jellyfin's extended features such as notifications and webhooks.
    • Compatible with all Jellyfin clients —Web UI, Streamyfin for Android/iOS, Jellyfin Media Player, and even third-party clients such as Infuse and Swiftfin.

    This means you don't need to learn any new interfaces or workflows—everything remains the same, only the content has become "unlimited".

    III. Key Dependency: What is AIOStreams?

    Before you delve into deployment, you need to understand Gelato's core dependency— AIOStreams .

    AIOStreams is an open-source project maintained by developer Viren070github.com/Viren070/AIOStreams (GitHub: ), and its slogan is " One addon to rule them all".

    As of early 2026, AIOStreams had garnered over 1,400 stars on GitHub and maintained an active nightly update schedule.

    Why are AIOStreams needed?

    The traditional way to use Stremio is as follows: you need to install multiple plugins such as Torrentio, Comet, and MediaFusion, each with its own configuration interface, Debrid key input, filtering rules, etc., which is very cumbersome to manage.

    AIOStreams was created to solve this problem—it "wraps" all these source plugins in a unified configuration interface:

    AIOStreams is currently the only Stremio Manifest backend supported by Gelato. In other words, Gelato does not directly connect to Torrentio or Comet—it connects to everything indirectly through AIOStreams.

    Deployment methods of AIOStreams

    You have two options:

    1. Use a public instance (recommended for beginners)
      • ElfHosted offers free public instances:aiostreams.elfhosted.com
      • It has a reasonable rate limit, suitable for light use and experience.
      • Public instances do not allow direct addition of Torrentio by default, but it can be used indirectly by "wrapping" other public AIOStreams instances.
    2. Self-deployment (recommended for advanced users)
      • AIOStreams provides Docker images and supports self-hosting.
      • Self-hosting unlocks all features and has no rate limits.
      • You can freely add any Stremio plugin URL.

    IV. Introduction to Mainstream Strimio Source Plugins

    Understanding the full capabilities of Gelato requires familiarity with the Stremio plugin ecosystem. Below are some of the most popular Stremio source plugins as of early 2026, all of which can be integrated with Gelato through AIOStreams:

    Torrentio

    Torrentio is the oldest and most widely used plugin in the Stremio ecosystem, and has long been considered the "first plugin you must install when installing Stremio".

    • Data source : Aggregates data from multiple well-known torrent indexing sites, including YTS, EZTV, RARBG, 1337x, ThePirateBay, KickassTorrents, TorrentGalaxy, MagnetDL, NyaaSi, Rutracker, etc.
    • Configurable options : Supports filtering by sorting method, resolution, file size, etc.
    • Debrid Integration : Supports Real-Debrid, Premiumize, AllDebrid, etc., for obtaining high-speed HD links.
    • Stability issues : During 2025-2026, Torrentio frequently experienced outages or "No streams found" errors due to high server load. Therefore, it is strongly recommended to use it in conjunction with other plugins and not rely on Torrentio alone.

    Comet

    Comet is a new generation of Stremio plugin that prioritizes speed and flexibility , claiming to be "Stremio's fastest torrent/debrid search add-on".

    • The data sources are extremely rich : it supports more than ten Scraper software, including Jackett, Prowlarr, Torrentio, Zilean, MediaFusion, Debridio, StremThru, AIOStreams, Jackettio, TorBox, Nyaa, BitMagnet, TorrentsDB, Peerflix, DMM, and SeaDex.
    • Extensive Debrid Support : Real-Debrid, All-Debrid, Premiumize, TorBox, Debrid-Link, Debrider, EasyDebrid, OffCloud, PikPak
    • Proxy streaming : Supports 4K proxy streaming, allowing multiple devices/locations to share the same Debrid account.
    • Public Instances : ElfHosted offers free public Comet instances ( comet.elfhosted.com), and a paid Comet Premium version offers higher rate limits.
    • Local caching : Supports SQLite or PostgreSQL caching to speed up repeated queries.

    MediaFusion

    MediaFusion is a full-featured, "all-in-one" Stremio plugin , known as the "Universal Stremio Add-on".

    • Wide coverage : It supports not only movies and TV series, but also live TV, sports events, and IPTV channels —features that most other plugins lack.
    • Privacy protection : User data is encrypted; encrypted URLs are stored only on Stremio.
    • Parental controls : Built-in filtering function based on nudity level and content rating.
    • Live sports streaming : Provides live and replay of sports events through the DaddyLive HD platform.
    • Non-Torrent Sources : Unlike Torrentio, MediaFusion includes non-Torrent links, so you can find available sources even if the torrent index site is down.
    • Public instances : ElfHosted sponsored public instances ( mediafusion.elfhosted.com), with reasonable rate limits.

    Quick Comparison of Three Major Plugins

    Recommended strategy : Enable Comet + MediaFusion as the base configuration in AIOStreams , and Torrentio as a supplementary source. This achieves the best balance between coverage and stability.

    V. Why should you try gelato?

    Solving the anxiety of "movie shortage"

    Jellyfin's biggest pain point is **"no downloads, no content"**. You meticulously build the hardware and configure the server, but the size of your media library depends entirely on your hard drive capacity and how frequently you download.

    With the integration of Gelato, this limitation is completely broken—your media library is logically "infinite." Whether it's a newly released movie, a niche TV series, or a classic film you suddenly want to rewatch, as long as it's available in the Stremio ecosystem, you can search for and play it directly in Jellyfin. It's gone from "download first, then watch" to "search and play instantly."

    Unified search experience

    Before Gelato, your workflow might have looked like this:

    1. Open Jellyfin → Search → Nothing → Disappointed
    2. Open Stremio → Search → Find → View in Stremio
    3. Or open your download tool → download → wait → finally view it in Jellyfin

    With Gelato, the workflow becomes:

    1. Open Jellyfin → Search → It can find and play content regardless of whether it's locally available.

    One search box, all sources at once. The distinction between local and online resources has completely disappeared.

    Maintain the integrity of the Jellyfin ecosystem

    Unlike a complete migration to Stremio, Gelato allows you to remain within the Jellyfin ecosystem . This means:

    • All your accumulated playback history, favorites, and user settings will remain unaffected.
    • Your already configured Jellyfin clients (Jellyfin on TV, Streamyfin on mobile, etc.) can continue to be used normally.
    • Your Jellyfin user management and access control system remains unchanged.
    • You don't need to teach your family how to use a new app—they won't even be aware of Gelato's existence; they'll just wonder, "Why are there suddenly so many videos?"

    Debrid multi-device security

    As mentioned earlier, Gelato's proxy streaming mechanism naturally solves the multi-IP limitation problem of Debris services. For a household with multiple devices, this value is enormous— no more carefully managing Debris connections on each device .

    VI. How to deploy quickly?

    Prerequisites

    Before you begin, please make sure you meet the following conditions:

    • Jellyfin 10.11 or later is installed and running (this is a hard requirement for Gelato).
      • If you are currently using version 10.10.x, you must upgrade to 10.10.7 first, and then upgrade to 10.11.
      • Jellyfin 10.11 is a major update (migrating to the EF Core database engine), and a full backup is strongly recommended before upgrading.
    • Have at least one Debrid service account (such as Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, TorBox, etc.), or be willing to use P2P streaming (Beta feature).
    • AIOStreams Manifest URL is ready (using a public instance or self-hosted).

    Step 1: Configure AIOStreams

    1. Access the AIOStreams configuration page (public instance: aiostreams.elfhosted.com[example address], or your self-hosted address](link)
    2. In the Debrid Services section, configure your Debrid Service API Key.
      • If multiple Debrid services are used, they are ordered by priority (AIOStreams will prioritize retaining the results of the services ranked first during deduplication).
    3. Enable the required Stremio plugin in the plugin marketplace.
      • Minimum requirements : TMDB plugin enabled (for search and metadata) + at least one plugin that provides streaming (Comet recommended).
      • Recommended configuration : TMDB + Comet + MediaFusion
    4. Reduce the default timeout : Set the timeout for the Stremio plugin in AIOStreams to around 5 seconds for faster response times.
    5. Save the configuration and record the generated Manifest URL.

    Step 2: Install the Gelato plugin

    1. Log in to the Jellyfin management dashboard.
    2. Go to Plugins → Repositories

    3. Add a new plugin repository with the following URL:

      https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lostb1t/Gelato/refs/heads/gh-pages/repository.json
    4. After refreshing the page, find and install Gelato in the **Plugins Directory (Catalog)**.
    5. Restart the Jellyfin server (this step is essential).

    Step 3: Create a dedicated media library folder for Gelato

    This step is one that many beginners easily overlook, but it is very important:

    1. Create a new folder on your server specifically for Gelato's virtual media library.
      • For example: /media/gelato-moviesand/media/gelato-shows
      • Never use an existing local media library folder! Gelato requires a separate folder to store virtual entries.
    2. Create new media libraries in Jellyfin, pointing to these new folders.
    3. Choose TMDB as the metadata downloader (do not use TVDB, as it may cause abnormal behavior).

    Step 4: Configure the Gelato plugin

    1. In the Jellyfin admin panel, go to Plugins → Gelato settings page.
    2. In the Streamio URL field, paste the AIOStreams Manifest URL you obtained in step one.
    3. In the Base Path field, add the path to the folder created in step three.
    4. Optional settings :
      • If you already have a local media library and do not want duplicate results during searches, you can uncheck "Enable Stream Results and Local Files".
      • For the TV series library, enable "Gelato missing season/episode fetcher" and place it at the top of the metadata downloader.

    Step 5: Start using

    Once configured, you have two ways to start experiencing it:

    1. Direct Search : Search for any movie title in Jellyfin, and Gelato will automatically return results from the Stremio source.
    2. To import catalog items : Locate "Import Catalog Items" in Jellyfin's Scheduled Tasks , and run it manually or set an automatic execution interval.

    All done! Now open your Jellyfin, search for a movie that's not on your hard drive, and experience the feeling of an "unlimited media library"!

    VII. Precautions and Frequently Asked Questions

    Compatibility Notes

    • Jellyfin Enhanced Plugin Conflict : If you have the Jellyfin Enhanced plugin installed, it may automatically add all search results to your media library, causing unexpected behavior. It is recommended to disable Jellyfin Enhanced when using Gelato.
    • TVDB Plugin Issue : As mentioned earlier, using TVDB as a metadata downloader may cause errors. Please use TMDB instead.
    • Gelato does not store data : Gelato itself does not maintain a separate database; all data is written to Jellyfin's native database. If problems occur, you can use Gelato's Purge Task to clean up all Gelato-injected entries and start over.
    • Each time you modify the AIOStreams configuration, you need to restart Jellyfin for the changes to take effect.

    Performance optimization suggestions

    • Keep the table of contents concise : Don't be greedy—the more tables of contents, the slower the import process and the more random and irrelevant content appears. Using a curated selection list like Trakt/MDBList is a better solution.
    • Reduce timeouts : Set the plugin timeout in AIOStreams to 5 seconds to prevent slow sources from dragging down the overall experience.
    • To avoid problematic plugins : Debridio TMDB and Debridio TVDB have been reported to have issues by the community. It is recommended to use the standard TMDB plugin instead.

    P2P streaming (Beta)

    Gelato's support for P2P (peer-to-peer) streaming is currently in Beta. This means that even if you don't have a Debris service, you can still try using Gelato, but the experience may not be as stable or smooth as with a Debris solution. If you just want to try out Gelato's features, P2P mode is a zero-cost way to get started.

    8. Gelato's ecological niche: a comparison with related tools

    To help you make a more informed choice, Gelato is compared to other related tools below:

    Gelato vs. directly using Stremio

    In conclusion , if you're already using Jellyfin, Gelato is the best choice for extending its capabilities. If you don't need a local media library, Stremio is simpler to use directly.

    Gelato vs. Stremio-Jellyfin / Jellio+

    There are also "reverse" integration tools in the community—instead of importing Stremio content into Jellyfin, they import Jellyfin content into Stremio:

    • stremio-jellyfin (by akarazniewicz): A Stremio plugin that lets you access the Jellyfin media library within Stremio.
    • Jellio+ : Similar functionality, displays matching results from the Jellyfin server when searching in Stremio.

    These tools are oriented opposite to gelato:

    The choice depends on which platform's user experience you prefer. If you're already a heavy user of Jellyfin and have a large amount of local media, Gelato is a more natural choice.

    IX. Summary: Is it right for you?

    Use the checklist below to quickly determine if gelato is right for your needs:

    Gelato expands the capabilities of Jellyfin from within, allowing your private media library to evolve from "limited hard drive" to "unlimited streaming" through a small server-side plugin, with almost no changes to your usage habits.

    For users who have already invested time and effort in setting up a Jellyfin media server, the combination of Gelato + AIOStreams is arguably one of the most practical and valuable evolutionary solutions for self-built multimedia in 2025-2026. It allows you to maintain the integrity of your local media library while gaining the same "unlimited content" experience as Stremio users.

    Gelato—the name of a spoonful of ice cream—brings the sweetness of an entire streaming universe.
